text:
sara_support: Ashley from Acme hit us — stream cuts out mid-generation after they move from guest WiFi -> corporate SSID. Customer sees partial output then a 502 from our edge. They're worried about billing for partial tokens.

ashley_customer: yep, was streaming a long summary. It printed ~40% then client shows "502 Bad Gateway" and stream ends. No error body. happened twice. macOS app.

sara_support: ugh, can you paste client log snippet and repro steps? Also which model/route?

ashley_customer: model=gpt-large, route=/v1/stream, SDK=webview in-house wrapper. Repro: 1) start stream on guest wifi 2) switch to corporate SSID (requires web auth/captive portal) 3) stream stops. Have a short client log: 

```
network: switching from 10.10.0.45 -> 172.16.2.14
http: received status 302 redirect to http://captive.acme/login
sse: onmessage chunk #12
sse: connection closed, code=0, reason="EOF"
err: net::ERR_ABORTED
```

ashley_customer: billing question too — were we charged full? reported token count looks full but output truncated.

sara_support: adding @dev_jay and @tom_sre to triage. Also linking the customer ticket: #9872.

dev_jay: likely captive portal / HTTP redirect in the middle of a chunked SSE connection. Browser/client sees 302 and terminates socket. Our ingress (edge proxy) returns 502 when backend stream terminates unexpectedly. Not seeing auth token TTL here yet.

ashley_customer: is there any way to avoid partial billing? can we get a pro-rated credit?

support_bot: Billing policy: partial responses still bill tokens that were generated server-side. Escalation possible if outage on our side.

tom_sre: can you provide the edge request_id from the failed stream? we'll pull upstream logs and proxy traces. Also what user-agent + IP? Need NAT change evidence.

ashley_customer: request_id=rid_6f7a2b, user-agent=AcmeApp/1.4.2, last-client-ip=10.10.0.45 -> new-ip 172.16.2.14.

dev_jay: repro is straightforward: captive portal causing an HTTP 302 to login page mid-stream. Two failure modes: 1) client aborts, we see broken pipe and partial output, 2) some HTTP proxies return 502 to client. For the SDK: we should detect 3xx during streaming and surface a specific error (captive_portal_redirect) so apps can trigger reauth and resume with a new request.

ingrid_prod: from infra side, we see rid_6f7a2b: backend stream produced tokens until chunk 12 then connection reset by peer. Edge emitted 502 after a 1s retry window. No internal model error.

dev_jay: suggested mitigations: 
- client: detect network change / 3xx and attempt reconnect with reauth (resume not possible since SSE is stateless for server stream).
- server: change edge behavior to surface a 491 or 420-style code for mid-stream network errors? (so clients can differentiate).
- docs: add captive-portal troubleshooting note.

ashley_customer: any short-term workaround for us? Clients are users in airports and conference centers.

tom_sre: short term: increase client keepalive and catch 3xx events in the webview; if you see 302 to login page, abort gracefully and reopen stream after auth. We can add a header check on our edge to detect upstream 302 to captive portal and return X-Edge-Note: captive_redirect to make automated detection easier. Need product OK.

dev_jay: repro commands for engineering testing (SSE):
```
# simulate long SSE stream
curl -N -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" "https://api.redwood.example/v1/stream?model=gpt-large" \ 
  | pv -qL 100 > /dev/null
# while running, trigger a 302 from a local proxy to emulate captive portal
```

dev_jay: client log snippet showing the error mapping we see in many cases: 
```
[SSE] event: data chunk (partial)
[SSE] event: data chunk (partial)
[NET] event: remote HTTP/1.1 302 Found Location: http://captive.local/login
[SSE] error: connection closed by peer
[ERR] net::ERR_HTTP2_PROTOCOL_ERROR
```

ingrid_prod: filing infra ticket INF-2319 to add edge header on detected upstream redirects and to keep a short trace for billing disputes.

support_bot: Created INF-2319 and BUG-889 for SDK detection heuristics.

sara_support: Action items: 1) ask customer to implement short-term client detection + reconnect steps (see above); 2) infra to add edge header (INF-2319); 3) SDK team to add detection & clearer error (BUG-889).

ashley_customer: ok we'll try the client change and follow up if we still see 502s. appreciate the triage. :pray:

dev_jay: one extra note — if you need to preserve tokens for partial generation, consider chunked checkpoints on the app side (save partial output and resume generating next chunks in a fresh request). Not ideal but helps UX.

tom_sre: flagging for billing team: if customer provides proof of captive portal redirect mid-stream and our edge shows no backend fault, we can evaluate a one-off credit.

sara_support: thanks team. closing loop when customer confirms. :white_check_mark:
